$comment: Rekey vocabulary — Mitchell/platform estimate wording mapped to CCC ONE
keying vocabulary and CIECA EMS v2.01 codes.
Universality directive: this file holds PLATFORM vocabulary only. No
carrier, shop, make, model, claim or RO literal may ever appear here.
Knowing that 'Remove / Replace' is CCC's 'Repl' is estimating-platform
data, the same way operationAliases.json knows cross-carrier wording.
Aliases are matched on the NORMALIZED form: uppercased, punctuation
collapsed to single spaces, whitespace collapsed. Write them that way.
Operation aliases are anchored at the START of a row description, longest
alias first, so a description word can never be read as an operation.
ADDITIVE-ONLY. Estimators extend this file directly; no code change is
required. Anything not listed resolves to UNMAPPED and is carried through
verbatim and flagged for the estimator — it is never guessed.
$targetTermsComment: A "mitchell" term beside a "ccc" one is the word the OTHER platform's print uses for the same operation or part type — the name an estimator keying into that platform types. Read off the two real Mitchell estimates in this repository, which between them print these nine operations and five part types. An entry with no "mitchell" term has none in evidence (CAPA A/M and Recond appear on neither print) and is reported as untranslated rather than guessed. "mitchellCharge" is a second word for one CCC operation: Mitchell prints a manual line as "Additional Cost" where it carries a charge and no hours (its $912.00 materials line) and "Additional Operation" where it bills hours (Clear Coat, Cover Car).
$operationsAliasesKeptInDescriptionComme: An alias that names the operation but STAYS in the description. A word in an operation column is an operation; the same word at the head of a description may be part of the description, and one document settles which: a CCC print writes "Rpl information labels" with an EMPTY operation column, and that estimate's own EMS export stores all three words as LINE_DESC. Taking "Rpl" out left the row reading "information labels", which matched the export's section-heading line instead of its own and reported a labor delta that was not there. So the operation is read and the wording is left exactly as the source keeps it.
$operationsLaneCommentary: Two facts about the operation CODES an export writes on labor lanes, both measured on the exports here. refinishLane: the operation can be the operation OF a refinish lane — every LAR lane these exports code carries OP6 (refinish), OP15 (blend), OP14 (clear coat, which this table does not name) or OP0 (manual), with one exception. partOperation: the operation acts on a PART, so it cannot describe a labor lane on a line that has no part. The exception is where the two meet: one platform repeats a LINE's code on every labor lane of the line — three of its lines carry OP11 on their body lane AND on their refinish lane — and it writes that same OP11 on a prep line that has a refinish lane, no part number and no price. There the code is the code of the line the prep belongs to, and it contradicts nothing about the prep.
$operationsLaborOpCodesSeenComment: Codes an export has been SEEN to write for this operation, as against laborOpCode, which is the one code this build writes. The two lists differ because one platform declines to code what the other codes: it writes no code at all on its own refinish, overhaul and aim lines, so those entries write nothing and read what the other platform writes. Every code here was matched line by line against the print that produced the export — OP5 on its one overhaul line ("Frt Bumper Cover Assy", the print says Overhaul), OP8 on its one aim line ("Headlamps", Check Adjust), OP6 on all seven of its refinish lanes, OP13 on the materials line the print files as an Additional Cost, and OP14 on the five it files as Additional Operations — which are the two halves of the one operation this table calls Manual. Reading a code is not writing one: nothing here changes what an export this build produces contains.

partTypes.$emsAliasesComment: Codes a real export writes for a line that buys no part. Mitchell writes PART_TYPE "PAE" on the lines its print types "Existing" — the overhaul and R&I lines that bill labor against a part already on the vehicle. CCC writes "PAO" on the R&I and align lines that name the part they work on ("RT Side support", part 5211506050, R&I 0.1 h, no price) and on its sublet charge lines; its own print states no part type on either, and neither is a part type an estimator keys.

$knownCccGroupsComment: The CCC group names, read off real CCC documents rather than assumed: the group headings a CCC print heads its line bands with, and the LINE_REF=0 heading rows a CCC EMS export carries in its .lin table. Both sources are in tests/fixtures. Groups this repository has not yet seen in a real CCC document keep their place in the order but are not evidence of CCC's own wording.
$cccLaborMarkersComment: The letter a CCC print puts beside a line's hours to say which labor type they are. Taken from the abbreviation legend the estimate prints on its own last page: B=BODY LABOR D=DIAGNOSTIC E=ELECTRICAL F=FRAME G=GLASS M=MECHANICAL P=PAINT LABOR S=STRUCTURAL.
$groupOrderComment: Print order, taken from the sequence two real CCC documents put their groups in (a CCC estimate print and a CCC EMS export for a different claim, which agree wherever they overlap). Groups neither document carries keep their earlier relative order, placed where they contradict neither.

totalsCategories.label: Parts adjustments
totalsCategories.note: A parts markup. An EMS export states markup per line rather than as a subtotal, so the export has no figure to compare this against.

totalsCategories.label: Parts
totalsCategories.note: The export's parts total rolls up new, other and SUBLET parts; whatever it carries as sublet is also on the sublet row.

totalsCategories.label: Materials total
totalsCategories.note: A print states refinish materials as ONE line billed on its refinish units; an export splits the same money by stage. The printed line answers to the materials TOTAL: on the CCC estimate measured here, $756.00 paint + $66.00 two-stage + $216.00 blend is the $1,038.00 it prints. Where a print states a stage of its own — shop materials on a Mitchell totals page — that stage is netted out of this comparison so the same dollars are not counted on two rows.

totalsCategories.label: Shop materials
totalsCategories.note: The shop-materials line. Both exports here bill it in units at a $0.00 rate, so it carries hours and no dollars.

totalsCategories.label: Two-stage materials
totalsCategories.note: A materials line inside the materials total, billed at the paint-materials rate. The code's expansion is read from the code family; the reference packet lists it without a description.

totalsCategories.label: Blend materials
totalsCategories.note: A materials line inside the materials total, billed at the paint-materials rate. The code's expansion is read from the code family; the reference packet lists it without a description.

totalsCategories.label: UPD
totalsCategories.note: The export carries this under a group code with no category and no counterpart on the source's totals page. This build has no evidence for what it means, so it is reported as printed rather than named.

totalsCategories.label: Paint materials
totalsCategories.note: The paint stage of the materials total. A print that states one materials line is compared against the total rather than against this stage alone.

$estimatingSystemsComment: The code an EMS export writes in .env EST_SYSTEM, against the platform whose print this build reads. Read off real exports: both CCC exports here carry "C", the Mitchell export carries "M", and that estimate's BMS names the same vendor with VendorCode "M". A code this table does not know is left unresolved rather than guessed.

$comment: MOTOR <-> CEG part nomenclature (WO-RK1 v3).
The two estimating databases name the same physical part differently:
MOTOR prints 'Side support' where CEG prints 'Frt Bumper Cover Support'.
Keyed correctly, those are the SAME line, but they key differently and
the verification pass reported each of them twice — once as never keyed
and once as keyed but absent from the source. This table pairs them.
Database vocabulary only, same universality directive as the rest of
this file: no carrier, shop, make, model, claim or RO literal.
'scope' restricts an entry to one CCC group so a generic word
('Protector') cannot rewrite a line in an unrelated section. An UNMAPPED
group on either side satisfies any scope. 'fixture' names the document
that proved the pairing — entries are earned from a document, never
assumed. Synonyms are written in the normalized form (uppercased,
punctuation collapsed); side words and the noise tokens below are
removed before the table is consulted, so write the bare part name.
